title: Kattalan Just Opened in Four Languages. It Has a ₹50 Crore Budget, Ravi Basrur's Score, and a Direct Line to Marco.
excerpt: Antony Varghese's biggest film yet extends Malayalam cinema's action universe to a pan-Indian stage — with ivory smuggling, a hunter's revenge, and the KGF composer behind the chaos.
body:
Malayalam cinema's appetite for ultraviolent, myth-scaled action has not slowed down since Marco. If anything, it has accelerated.

Kattalan — which translates roughly to "hunter" — opened today across India in Malayalam, Telugu, Hindi, and Kannada. It is the most expensive film Antony Varghese has ever been part of, carrying a reported budget of ₹50 crore. For context, Marco, the film whose universe Kattalan extends, was made for a fraction of that.

## The Marco Connection

Director Paul George has not been subtle about the link. Kattalan is set in Aanakolli, a fictional territory controlled by a criminal syndicate involved in ivory smuggling — the same trade that surfaced as a subplot in Marco. A kidnapping thread from the earlier film reappears here, unresolved and now central.

Unni Mukundan, who led Marco, has clarified that he is not part of Kattalan and has distanced himself from the term "cinematic universe." But the connective tissue is visible to anyone watching both films. Malayalam cinema appears to be building something — not through post-credits scenes and franchise maps, but through shared criminal economies and overlapping underworlds.

## Ravi Basrur's Score Carries the Film

If there is one element drawing unanimous praise from early audiences, it is the background score. Ravi Basrur — the man behind the seismic soundscapes of KGF and KGF: Chapter 2 — composed the music for Kattalan, and his presence is immediately felt. Social media reactions from opening day screenings have singled out the BGM as the film's strongest element, with several viewers comparing it favorably to Basrur's Kannada work.

The rest of the reception has been more divided. BookMyShow audiences have given the film a 7.7 out of 10 rating. Critics have praised the action choreography — which includes international stunt teams — while noting that the screenplay does not always match the ambition of the production design. Evening occupancy on Day 1 landed at 40.17%, well below Drishyam 3's 71% opening in the same market, but respectable for a film without a legacy franchise behind it.

## Antony Varghese's Bet

Varghese, who broke through with the scrappy indie Angamaly Diaries in 2017, has called Kattalan the biggest film of his career. He is not exaggerating. The film features Dushara Vijayan — best known for Asuran opposite Dhanush — making her Malayalam debut. The supporting cast includes veterans Siddique and Jagadish, alongside Telugu actor Sunil in a role that signals the film's pan-Indian ambitions.

The multilingual release is significant. Malayalam cinema has traditionally relied on subtitled theatrical runs and OTT windows to reach audiences beyond Kerala. Kattalan is attempting a Day 1 dubbed release across South and North India — a strategy that worked spectacularly for Drishyam 3 and has become the new default for Malayalam films with crossover potential.

## What This Means for the Diaspora

For the Kerala diaspora — one of the most cinema-obsessed communities in the Indian population abroad — Kattalan represents a test. Can a Malayalam action film without a Mohanlal or a Mammootty in the lead drive overseas audiences to theatres?

Early reports from the Gulf and North America suggest moderate interest. The film does not have the name recognition of Drishyam or the novelty of Marco's first-mover status. But if word of mouth around Basrur's score and the Marco connection gains traction over the weekend, Kattalan could find its audience in the same way KGF did — not through star power, but through sheer sonic and visual intensity.

The first weekend numbers will tell the real story. Malayalam cinema's action universe is expanding. Whether it can sustain the expansion depends on what audiences in Kochi, Dubai, Dallas, and Toronto decide over the next 72 hours.
